statement: The moving-boundary quasi-stationary literature exists, it is Ocafrain's, and it excludes this process for a precise reason. READ AT SOURCE 16 September 2026. Three papers bear on the laboratory's object. (1) Ocafrain, Quasi-stationarity and quasi-ergodicity for DISCRETE-TIME Markov chains with absorbing boundaries moving PERIODICALLY, ALEA 15:429-451 (2018), arXiv:1707.08419. (2) Ocafrain, Q-processes and asymptotic properties of Markov processes conditioned not to hit moving boundaries, Stochastic Process. Appl. 130(6):3445-3476 (2020). (3) Ocafrain, An ergodic theorem for asymptotically periodic time-inhomogeneous Markov processes, with application to quasi-stationarity with moving boundaries, arXiv:2010.05483, Adv. Appl. Probab. WHAT (1) GIVES THE LABORATORY, AND IT IS REAL. Proposition 2.1, verbatim: 'Assume there exist l, m in Z_+ such that A_l is not A_m. Then there is no measure nu in P(E) satisfying for all n, P_nu(X_n in . | tau > n) = nu(.).' So as soon as the killing boundary moves at all there is NO quasi-stationary distribution in the strict sense. The laboratory's phase-indexed family Pi_phi is therefore forced rather than chosen, and that is now a citable theorem instead of an observation. Theorem 1.4 then gives existence of the QUASI-ERGODIC distribution -- the limit of the time average, Definition 1.3 -- for a FINITE state space with a gamma-periodic boundary, proved by reducing to a periodic chain and extending Darroch and Seneta (1965) from the aperiodic case. The capped rational-barrier walk is exactly that object, so for fixed q and fixed cap the existence question is elementary finite Perron-Frobenius and citable. The paper closes with random walks absorbed by 2-periodic boundaries. WHY IT DOES NOT REACH US. The finiteness in (1) is load-bearing; the half-line is not covered. The general moving-boundary theory in (2) and (3) runs on Assumption (A'), a conditional Doeblin condition (A'1) plus a Harnack-like survival comparison (A'2), and (3) states that in the time-homogeneous framework this IS the Champagnat-Villemonais condition, 'shown as being equivalent to the exponential uniform convergence to quasi-stationarity in total variation'. This process converges POLYNOMIALLY -- d^-1 to the limit, d^-2 between runs, with no exponential weight restoring a spectral gap (no_weight_separates, Lean) -- so (A') provably fails here. The driven theory covers the non-critical regime and the critical regime is exactly what it excludes. WHAT THIS CORRECTS, AND IT IS MY OWN NARROWING. J-yaglom-rate-is-one-over-d narrowed the driven-critical gap to 'driven-and-lattice, not driven-and-critical', on the ground that Ocafrain ECP 2020 supplies the criticality with the right rate. That is true only for a FIXED boundary. With the moving-boundary papers read, the driven half is covered only under exponential uniformity, so the uncovered combination is driven-AND-critical after all, as the original entry said. The narrowing was too optimistic and the negative-knowledge entry is corrected. Also corrected: that entry's instruction that there is 'not one to find' is too strong -- there is a literature, it is precisely locatable, and what it lacks is precisely statable. No bound moves.

Rhin equation (8) cannot be used: it is conditional on H >= H_0 with H_0 declared effectively computable and never computed. READ AT SOURCE 16 September 2026 from the Seminaire de Theorie des Nombres Paris 1985-86 scan, p. 160. The Proposition: 'Soient u_0, u_1, u_2 trois entiers tels que H = max(|u_1|,|u_2|) >= 2. Alors la forme Lambda = u_0 + u_1 log 2 + u_2 log 3 verifie (7) |Lambda| >= H^(-13,3). De plus pour H >= H_0 (H_0 effectivement calculable) (8) |Lambda| >= H^(-7,616).' THE ERRAND'S ANSWER IS NO, and it closes the row permanently: L^8.616 is unreachable without H_0, and by J-wuwang-effectivity-is-a-saddle-point-cost H_0 = exp(Theta(n_0)), astronomically above the L of order 10^6 a cycle search reaches. Rhin (8) therefore joins Wu-Wang in the ineffective pile for exactly the same reason, and the effective threshold stays L^14.3. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE LABORATORY'S RECORD. First, both (7) and (8) are the THREE-TERM form u_0 + u_1 log2 + u_2 log3 with H = max(|u_1|,|u_2|), which confirms J-rhin-eight-readings-are-one-theorem at source -- that row was reconstructed from Zudilin and Spiegelhofer and is now read. Second, Rhin's (7) carries NO CONSTANT: it is |Lambda| >= H^(-13,3) outright for H >= 2. The 915 belongs to Simons-de Weger's Lemma 12, not to Rhin. The chain is unaffected but the attribution in the audit table was loose. THE CONSTRUCTION IS PRINTED AND CHECKS OUT. Appendix 2, p. 162: to prove (8) one studies the integrals of H_n(x)/x^(n+1) over [2,3] and over [3,4], with H_n(x) = 12^7 times the product of Q_i(x)^[b_i n] for Q_1 = x-3 (b_1 = 0.704324), Q_2 = x-2 (0.552418), Q_3 = x-4 (0.447582), Q_4 = 5x-12 (0.109072), Q_5 = 17x^2-102x+144 (0.038934), Q_6 = 19x^2-108x+144 (0.054368). Two independent checks confirm the transcription. The degree identity sum b_i deg Q_i = 2.000000 exactly, matching the requirement deg H_n <= 2n on p. 159 -- six six-decimal numbers hitting an integer constraint. And the Laplace rates of the two integrals agree to 7.3e-6 (-1.50975980 on [2,3] at x = 2.223575, -1.50976709 on [3,4] at x = 3.652850), which is the signature of the Smyth-style balanced optimisation Rhin describes on p. 161. THE SCAN'S ONE AMBIGUOUS CHARACTER WAS SETTLED BY THE MATHEMATICS: the 12^7 factor was first read as 12^(7n), but an n there makes the rate +15.8846 and the integrals diverge, so the exponent is a constant 7. WHAT DOES NOT MOVE: no bound, no floor, no fate. What moves is that an unverified external row is now verified and dead rather than unverified and hopeful.

The Rhin equation (8) dispute dissolves: the two 'incompatible' readings are two corollaries of one linear independence measure, and BOTH are right. THE EVIDENCE, read at first hand 16 September 2026. Spiegelhofer arXiv:2105.11173v2 defines alpha = log3/log2 on p. 1 and writes on p. 2: 'a bound for the irrationality measure mu(alpha) of alpha ... was given by Rhin [48, Equation (8)]: we have mu(alpha) <= 8.616. Also, Wu and Wang [60] obtained the bound mu(log 3) <= 5.1163051.' So the laboratory's transcription is exact and he does mean the ratio. Zudilin arXiv:math/0404523 section 3.4, p. 13: 'To derive a nice irrationality measure for log 3, Rhin constructs in [Rh2] SIMULTANEOUS APPROXIMATIONS TO a_1 = 2/3, a_2 = 4/3 ... By these means he proves Theorem 3. The irrationality exponent of gamma in Q log 2 + Q log 3 satisfies the inequality mu(gamma) < 8.616.' THE RESOLUTION. Simultaneous approximation to log(2/3) and log(4/3) is a linear independence measure for (1, u, v) with u = log2 - log3 and v = 2log2 - log3. That change of basis is INTEGRAL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- log2 = v - u and log3 = v - 2u -- so ZZ + ZZu + ZZv and ZZ + ZZlog2 + ZZlog3 are the SAME LATTICE, and a measure for one is a measure for the other with the same exponent and H changed by at most a factor 2. From that one measure |a + b log2 + c log3| >= c' H^(-7.616-eps): setting a = 0 gives |q log3 - p log2| >= c' H^(-7.616-eps), hence mu(log3/log2) <= 8.616, which is Spiegelhofer; setting b = 0 gives mu(log 3) <= 8.616, which is how Wu-Wang p. 265 cite it; and gamma in Q log2 + Q log3 gives Zudilin's Theorem 3. Three corollaries, one theorem. The audit's framing -- 'the two readings are incompatible; only one can be equation (8)' -- is a false dichotomy, and the reason it looked like one is that Zudilin states a corollary that happens to EXCLUDE the ratio while the theorem under it does not. Nobody is in error. SAME ARCHITECTURE AS WU-WANG, verified at source the day before: Theorem 1 three-term, Corollary 1 the two-term headline. Rhin is built the same way, which is what should have been expected. WHAT REMAINS, and it is now a bound question rather than a reading question: equation (8)'s CONSTANT. Rhin's title is 'mesures EFFECTIVES d'irrationalite' and the laboratory already uses equation (7) effectively with constant 915, so (8) is very likely effective too, but its constant is not recorded anywhere reachable. If it is explicit, Paper A's effective cycle threshold improves from L^14.3 to L^8.616 -- and by J-wuwang-effectivity-is-a-saddle-point-cost that would be the best EFFECTIVE bound available, since Wu-Wang's 5.1163051 supplies nothing at any reachable L. p. 160 is still unread and is now worth reading for the constant alone.

H_0(eps) of Wu-Wang Theorem 1 is NOT computed here; it is reduced to its inputs, and the reduction says the prime-number part is cheap and the saddle-point part is the whole cost. THE TRANSFER, explicitly. Hata's Lemma 4 applied to r_n = d D_n Q_n A_1 and eps_n^(t) = d D_n Q_n I_n(d/2, s_t): r_n Lambda = [p r_n + q_1 P_n^(1) + q_2 P_n^(2)] + q_1 eps_n^(1) + q_2 eps_n^(2), the bracket an integer, so when it is nonzero and n is chosen minimal with H(|eps_n^(1)| + |eps_n^(2)|) <= 1/2 one gets |Lambda| >= 1/(2 r_n). With r_n <= e^((sigma+delta)n) and |eps_n^(t)| <= e^(-(tau-delta)n) valid for n >= n_0(delta), n = ceil(log(4H)/(tau-delta)) gives |Lambda| >= (1/2)(4H)^(-(sigma+delta)/(tau-delta)). Hence the exponent is nu(delta) = (sigma+delta)/(tau-delta) and, crucially, H_0 = exp(Theta(n_0(delta))): the threshold is EXPONENTIAL in wherever the asymptotics become effective. THE THREE LIMITS, BY SOURCE. lim (1/n) log Q_n = 0.490974 log 2 is EXACT, Q_n being defined as a power of 2. lim (1/n) log d D_n = 1 is the prime number theorem. lim (1/n) log |A_1| = 4.513284 and lim (1/n) log |I_n| = -2.762369, -2.762389 are saddle point, and the paper states limits only. ONLY THE UPPER BOUND ON psi IS NEEDED, since r_n and eps_n both carry D_n in the numerator -- a simplification worth having. THE PNT PART IS CHEAP. An all-x bound psi(n) <= c n removes that threshold from n_0 entirely, at the cost of the exponent: c = 1.03883 gives nu = 4.259932 against 4.116307, moving the cycle closure threshold from L^5.116307 to L^5.259932. THE SADDLE POINT IS THE COST, and it is severe because H_0 is exponential in n_0. Even assuming the optimistic O(1/sqrt n) error shape, n_0 ~ delta^-2 gives H_0 ~ exp(8.2e3) at eps = 0.05, about 10^3500. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LABORATORY, and it is not currently recorded: the Wu-Wang supply of the Diophantine budget is asymptotic in a strong sense. For any period L a cycle search would reach, it supplies nothing, and Rhin equation (7) with its explicit constant 915 is what actually applies -- so L^14.3 is the effective statement and L^5.1163051 the asymptotic one. The Lean is unaffected: the budget is the hypothesis hWW. WHAT WOULD FINISH IT: explicit error terms for the two saddle-point asymptotics, which means redoing the analysis of I_n and A_1 with constants rather than limits. The arithmetic here was checked against the paper's own printed digits; nu = sigma/tau = 4.116307 against the stated bound 4.1163051, the difference being the truncation of the printed sigma and tau.

The Wu-Wang import is READ AT SOURCE and correct in every particular; the query raised against it on 15 September 2026 is withdrawn. THEOREM 1 of Wu and Wang, J. Number Theory 142 (2014) 264-273, p. 266, verbatim: for any eps > 0 there exists a positive integer H_0(eps) such that |p + q_1 log 2 + q_2 log 3| >= H^(-4.1163051-eps) for all integers p, q_1, q_2 with H = max(|q_1|, |q_2|) >= H_0(eps), where H_0(eps) is EFFECTIVELY COMPUTABLE. That is the three-term linear independence measure juggler_cycle_wuwang_reduction states, with the same exponent and the same H convention, so the substitution p = 0, q_1 = -L, q_2 = o giving Lambda = o log 3 - L log 2 >= L^(-4.1163051-eps) is exactly licensed. mu(log 3) <= 5.1163051 is Corollary 1, derived FROM Theorem 1 -- the two-term headline is the consequence and the three-term measure is the technical core, which is the structure the query wrongly assumed was absent. WHAT THE QUERY GOT RIGHT AND WRONG. Right: that a two-term measure cannot bound a form in two logarithms, and that the published headline is the two-term statement. Wrong: inferring from the headline what the paper proves. The failure mode was reasoning from a citation key and an abstract to a theorem, which is the same error as reading a secondary report for a primary source -- the error the audit already flags for Rhin equation (8). ONE REFINEMENT TO THE RECORD. The audit table lists Wu-Wang as effective 'no (C_eps)'. Theorem 1 asserts H_0(eps) is effectively computable, so the bound is effective in the technical sense; what the paper does not do is compute H_0(eps), so there is still no explicit companion to Rhin equation (7)'s 915. 'Effective but uncomputed' is the accurate entry, not 'not effective'. RHIN EQUATION (8) IS UNAFFECTED and still open: Wu-Wang p. 265 cites Rhin 1987 as giving mu(log 3) <= 8.616, a third reading consistent with Zudilin and with the log-3 literature, but it is still secondary and Spiegelhofer's explicit distinction between the two quantities in consecutive sentences is still unexplained. Rhin p. 160 remains unread. No bound moves: the threshold n >> L^5.1163051 stands where it already stood.
